mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Thursday, November 19, 2026. Let's start with the markets. Stocks were mixed on Wednesday. The Dow fell 561 points, or about 1.1 percent, to close near 50,198. The S&P 500 slipped about two tenths of a percent to around 7,324, dipping below its 200 day moving average. The Nasdaq bucked the trend, rising about four tenths of a percent to roughly 24,430. A sharp selloff in health insurers weighed on the Dow, while hawkish Fed minutes pushed the dollar higher. The ten year Treasury yield held near 5.1 percent. Stock futures were pointing higher early this morning. On the Fed, minutes from the October meeting, released Wednesday afternoon, showed that almost all officials judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate to bring inflation under control. At that meeting the Fed held its benchmark rate in a range of 3.75 to 4 percent, with two officials dissenting in favor of another hike. Futures markets now put the odds of a quarter point increase at the December meeting at roughly 95 percent. Earlier this week, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said several more hikes may be needed before next spring, while New York Fed President John Williams said conditions do not call for dramatic action. Next, health insurers had a rough second day. UnitedHealth fell about 10 percent and Humana about 13 percent after a federal proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits and recover more payments to the plans. Next, Anthropic priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars a share, above its earlier range. The deal raised about 81 billion dollars, making it the largest IPO on record and topping SpaceX's offering in June. Shares are set to begin trading on the Nasdaq today under the ticker A N T. Stocks of its big backers, including Amazon and Alphabet, rose on Wednesday. Next, Nvidia reported third quarter revenue of about 116 billion dollars, more than double a year ago, and guided to about 130 billion for the current quarter. An early gain faded, and the stock closed down nearly 3 percent. And finally, retailers had a good day. TJX, the parent of T J Maxx, jumped 8 percent after strong comparable sales and a raised outlook, and Target rose 4 percent after lifting its full year sales forecast. On the calendar today, Walmart reports before the bell, with Intuit, Ross Stores, Gap, Williams Sonoma, and Alibaba also on deck. On the data side, watch weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey this morning. Here's your fun fact. The oldest known share of stock in the world was not found in a bank vault, but in a small town archive in the Netherlands in 2010, discovered by a history student. It is a Dutch East India Company share dated 1606, issued to a man from Enkhuizen named Pieter Harmensz for 150 guilders. Trading in those same shares eventually helped give rise to the Amsterdam stock exchange. Have a great day.
